rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's eighteen builder trees go (a row of jacarandas, ficus and magnolias along the back fences, three jacarandas 3 m from the house fronts, a few in the yards inside the wrought-iron fence); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: on the open lot corner, by the potted plants, and in yards 5-14 m from the houses.

trees.why: the open lot corner inside the wrought-iron fence, 32 m from the walls: a full magnolia
the yard south of it, 12 m from the house, 31 m from the magnolia
the middle yard by the bird of paradise, 13.5 m from the house
the south back yard by the potted plants: the yard's tree
the east back yard of the south row, 5.5 m from the house: the one tree of the old back fence row there
